The committee met on Tuesday in the upper room of the market hall. The minutes of the previous
meeting were read and approved without amendment. The secretary reported that the new weights and
measures had been delivered by the carrier and were now stored in the cellar beneath the hall. It
was agreed that the inspector should examine them before they were issued to the traders, and that
a notice should be posted at the market cross informing the public of the change. The question of
the stall rents was raised by several members, who argued that the present charges were too high
for the smaller traders and drove them to sell in the street instead. After some discussion it was
resolved to reduce the charge for the smallest stalls by one third for a trial period of six months,
and to review the effect of the change at the end of that period. The treasurer was instructed to
keep a separate account of the rents collected so that the committee could judge the result.
